vendor_sources.title: Geekbench 5 Pro Command Line Tool
facts: geekbench5 is the primary Linux command-line interface.
The default workload is the CPU benchmark.
--save supports retaining a native result file; .gb5 is the recommended extension.
Text and JSON exports are supported, and --help documents the installed tool.

vendor_sources.title: Installing Geekbench 5 on Linux
facts: The vendor documents extracting the Linux archive and invoking the bundled geekbench5 executable.

vendor_sources.title: Frequently Asked Questions
facts: Scores from different major Geekbench versions are not comparable.
Other running applications and low-power mode can lower scores.
vendor_sources.inference: Do acquisition and provenance preparation in parallel, but obtain calibration on a host admitted for an uncontended benchmark; an artificially low score would improperly loosen the runtime allowance.

vendor_sources.title: Geekbench 5 Pro Standalone Mode
vendor_sources.retrieval: curl HTTPS GET after the browser tool could not retrieve this page
facts: The documented portable licensed mode requires a Geekbench 5 Pro license and supports an exported license file.
vendor_sources.limitation: The documentation alone does not prove that this host has a usable license or that an unregistered 5.5.1 build can complete the proposed offline invocation.

vendor_sources.title: Download Geekbench 7
facts: The general download page currently serves Geekbench 7; it is not the version-specific Geekbench 5 authority.

vendor_sources.title: Human Knowledge Compression Contest: Detailed Rules for Participation
facts: Each submitted program has a runtime bound based on the execution machine's Geekbench 5 score.
The local one-core objective uses a single-core score and applies the bound separately to compression and decompression.
vendor_sources.single_core_scope_authority: The one-core restriction and single-core score selection are bound by the local objective contract; the public rules also describe multicore reference scores.

download_authority.pending_binding: Retain the exact downloaded archive, response headers, byte count and computed SHA-256. Then bind every extracted executable and benchmark data file before any benchmark invocation. HTTP metadata is not a content checksum or proof of a qualifying result.

existing_source_bindings.role: Candidate-bound q1 full-corpus runtime plan; 11 direct implementation bindings match, but it is not an env8192 100M plan.

Consumes one raw report, verifies exact q1 A/B packages, fingerprints the current host, and runs full compression/decompression. It does not generate or bind the report-producing Geekbench executable.
Independently rederives one positive Geekbench 5 single-core score and current-host fingerprint for q1; report generation provenance must be supplied separately.

Historical opening-1M producer binds /usr/bin/geekbench5, --no-upload, a singleton CPU, owned cgroup, host and lease evidence. Candidate, paths, cgroup-parent inode and scope are fixed to v9; it cannot authorize a new 100M candidate.
Frozen opening-1M identity-only gate. Runtime and other resource eligibility remain N_A; a separately frozen 100M experiment is required.

required_future_authority_inputs: Exact vendor archive and download provenance, plus byte/SHA records for the actual executable and complete bundled benchmark runtime/data closure.
Retained --help/version output from the exact selected binary and proof that the chosen no-upload invocation is supported by the available installation/license.
An immutable command vector, environment, working directory, selected CPU, affinity/topology and host fingerprint captured with the benchmark execution.
A guarded, admitted benchmark invocation with raw stdout/stderr, successful exit status, native .gb5 result and exact hashes; no shared-host score borrowed from another machine.
Independent verification of exactly one positive single-core score identifying Geekbench 5, host identity, command and executable provenance, and clean guard/lease termination.
A separately frozen 100M env8192 successor that binds these inputs and its 1M exact-identity antecedent; runtime projections are reject-only and do not qualify a full-corpus submission.
